chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan narrated to me, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated to me from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah, who said: My father narrated to me from Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from Fadl ibn Yusuf, from Abdillah ibn Sinan, from Abi Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Whoever says twenty-five times every day: 'O Allah, forgive the believing men and believing women, the Muslim men and Muslim women,' Allah will write for him, for the number of every believer who has passed away and every believer who remains until the Day of Resurrection, one good deed; He will erase one bad deed from him and raise his rank.
ai.seo_question: What is the reward for reciting the supplication for believers twenty-five times a day?
ai.summary: In Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Thawab al-Amal*, this hadith highlights the communal dimension of individual piety, where a believer’s devotion is amplified by interceding for the entire Ummah. The promise of having sins erased and rank elevated serves as a powerful incentive for consistent dhikr, reflecting the Shia emphasis on the interconnectedness of the faithful across time. This practice underscores the belief that personal spiritual growth is inextricably linked to the well-being of the broader community of believers.
